headline: When to Replace Your Water Heater Gas Line
articleBody: Knowing when to replace your water heater's gas line can literally be a lifesaver, and it's definitely not something you want to guess about. While gas lines are built to last, they don't last forever, and certain signs point towards the need for a professional replacement. The most urgent sign is, of course, a gas leak – if you smell that 'rotten egg' odor, it's an immediate emergency that demands the gas be turned off and a professional called. Beyond leaks, visible damage like kinks, corrosion, or cracks on the line itself are huge red flags. Even if there's no active leak, a compromised line is a ticking time bomb. Another less obvious sign can be an old, inflexible gas connector, especially if it’s an aluminum or corrugated copper line, which are often not up to current safety codes and can fail over time. If you’re replacing an old water heater, it’s almost always a good idea to replace the gas line connector too, as the lifespan of the connector often mirrors that of the heater, and new heaters might have different requirements. Don't delay addressing these issues, as a failing gas line can lead to carbon monoxide poisoning, fire, or explosions.
